title: The GitHub repo everyone is using to mash up games with AI.
author: CelticVampire

comments.author: CelticVampire
comments.body:
​My last post about AI game crossovers got some solid discussion, so I wanted to share a quick follow-up for anyone curious about how people are actually pulling this off.

​It turns out someone built a dedicated toolkit specifically designed to let Claude Opus 5.5 handle the heavy lifting of cross-engine modding. I went up and searched for more information to see how it was actually working, and I stumbled on this exact GitHub repo that everyone on X is using to make these game mashups.

​It's an open-source project called Universal Modder, and it's built to help AI agents like Claude Code build wild mods for PC games you own. Instead of manual reverse-engineering, the tool uses the model to decompile game assets, resolve engine conflicts, and write the necessary translation scripts to fuse mechanics together. It even keeps a shared knowledge base so the AI can reuse discoveries from earlier mods.

https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder
